blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Closed-loop revision is increasingly adopted in large language model applications to iteratively reduce mismatches between generated outputs (e.g., a paragraph) and user targets (e.g., required paragraph length). However, revision failures may stem from incomplete feedback or models failing to act effectively on correct feedback, making it difficult to systematically assess the revision capabilities of LLMs. In this work, we propose a fixed-budget revision protocol in which deterministic verifiers report all remaining violations across three constraint families: exact-length, lexical, and compositional. This holds feedback correctness and completeness fixed, allowing us to isolate and evaluate model-side closed-loop revision. We conduct experiments on 19 mainstream open-source and closed-source models, including Llama 3.1 8B and GPT-5.6 Sol, and observe large cross-model and cross-constraint differences in final joint success, with controller-level mean final joint success ranging from 17.4% to 99.8%. Substantial cross-model gaps persist when the same initial draft is used. In controlled experiments, we find reproducible model-specific differences in how exact feedback is translated into revisions, while post-training and model scale reshape these responses without consistently bringing them closer to exact correction. Interestingly, across all constraint families, failure trajectories often repeat earlier outputs, and prior recurrence is associated with substantially lower subsequent recoverability. Finally, matched-state interventions across constraint families show that removing earlier dialogue, with the current draft and feedback fixed, changes recurrence escape without reliably improving final success; effects depend on the model, task, and trigger-state composition. Overall, exact feedback makes revision errors observable, but does not make the closed loop reliable. Code and reproduction instructions are available 1 1 1 https://github.com/kevinjiang0121-cyber/exact-feedback-code .
blocks.zh: 在大型语言模型应用程序中越来越多地采用闭路修订,以减少生成的产出(例如一段)与用户目标(例如所需段长)之间的不匹配。 然而,修订失败可能是由于反馈不完整或模型未能就正确的反馈采取有效行动,因此难以系统地评估法学硕士课程的修订能力。 在这项工作中,我们提议一项固定预算修订议定书,其中确定核查人员报告三个制约因素家庭的所有剩余侵权行为:准确长度、词汇和组成。 这使得反馈的正确性和完整性得到固定,使我们能够隔离和评估模型侧闭路修订。 我们进行19种主流开源模型和闭源模型的实验,包括Llama 3.1 8B和GPT-5.6 Sol,并观察到在最终联合成功中存在大的跨模型和跨约束性差异,控制层平均最终联合成功率从17.4%到99.8%不等. 在使用相同的初稿时,仍然存在重大的跨模式差距。 在有控制的实验中,我们发现在如何将准确的反馈转化为修订方面可以复制的模型特异性差异,而训练后和模型尺度则重新塑造了这些响应,而没有始终将它们更接近于精确的校正. 有趣的是,在所有制约因素的家族中,故障轨迹往往重复早先的产出,而先前的重复与随后的可恢复性大大降低有关。 最后,各种制约家庭的对应状态干预措施表明,在目前的草案和反馈得到固定的情况下,取消早先的对话会改变重现的逃逸情况,而不会可靠地改善最终的成功;效果取决于模式、任务和触发状态的构成。 总的来说,准确的反馈使得修订错误可以观察到,但并不能使闭环可靠. 代码和复制说明可查询11 1 https://github.com/kevinjiang0121-cyber/exact-feedback-code.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Feedback-driven revision is increasingly used in large language model (LLM) systems to bring
generated outputs closer to user requirements. Such systems revise behavior
across trials ( Shinn et al., 2023 ) , modify code using execution results ( Yang et al., 2024 ) , replan from environmental observations ( Huang et al., 2023 ) , and refine candidate programs using evaluator
scores ( Novikov et al., 2025 ) . In each setting, feedback identifies a
gap between the current output and the target, and LLMs must
decide how to act on it repeatedly and ultimately complete the task successfully.

However, revision can be unreliable due to a lack of reliable external feedback in
reasoning ( Huang et al., 2024 ) and inaccurate model-generated feedback by itself ( Olausson et al., 2024 ) .
Studies show that models can persist with
incorrect answers despite critiques ( Jiang et al., 2025 ) and
surveys further emphasize the role of feedback quality ( Kamoi et al., 2024 ) . When feedback itself may be unreliable, poor revision outcomes do not reveal whether the bottleneck lies in the feedback or in the model’s response to it. This leaves open how reliably LLMs can act on feedback over repeated revisions when that feedback is complete and correct.

blocks.en: In this work, we propose a trajectory-level framework to evaluate fixed-budget closed-loop revision in LLMs, as illustrated in Figure 1 . We study revision under explicit, deterministically checkable constraints and use verifiers that report all remaining violations after each revision. The same frozen rules generate feedback and determine final success, making feedback correctness and completeness controlled experimental conditions and allowing us to isolate model-side revision.
blocks.zh: 在这项工作中,我们提出了一个轨迹级别框架,用于评价法学硕士学位的固定预算闭关修订,如图1所示。 我们研究在明确、可核查的制约下进行修改,并使用核查员,在每次修改后报告所有剩余的违法行为。 同样的冻结规则产生反馈并确定最终成功,使反馈正确性和完整性控制了实验条件,并使我们能够隔离模型-侧面修订.

blocks.en: In particular, we build a reusable evaluation suite spanning three text-based constraint families—exact-length, lexical, and compositional—and use it to evaluate 19 mainstream open- and closed-source models. We first examine cross-model and cross-task variation, including fixed-draft comparisons that hold the starting response constant. We then characterize model-specific feedback-to-action responses under controlled correction requests, and test whether these patterns replicate on unseen texts and remain informative during independent multi-round revision. Finally, we analyze recurrent failure trajectories and use matched-state history interventions to examine how retained dialogue shapes subsequent editing behavior and final success.
blocks.zh: 特别是,我们建造了一个可重复使用的评价套件,涵盖三个基于文字的制约家庭——精确长度、词汇和组成——并利用它评价19个主流开放和封闭源码模式。 我们首先审查跨模型和跨任务变异,包括固定的草案比较,保持起始响应常数. 然后,我们根据有控制的更正请求,描述具体模式的反馈与行动反应,并测试这些模式是否复制在无形文本上,在独立多轮修订期间是否保持信息。 最后,我们分析反复出现的故障轨迹,并利用匹配的状态历史干预来审查保留的对话如何塑造随后的编辑行为和最终的成功.

blocks.en: Overall, our contributions and findings can be summarized as follows:
blocks.zh: 总之,我们的贡献和调查结果可归纳如下:

blocks.en: • An auditable framework and evaluation suite for isolating model-side revision. We introduce a fixed-budget request–model–verifier loop for closed-loop revision. Deterministic verifiers report all remaining violations and use the same frozen rules to determine final success, making feedback correctness and completeness controlled experimental conditions. The accompanying evaluation suite provides frozen cases, trajectory-level records, and generation and analysis pipelines for reproducible evaluation. • A systematic characterization of closed-loop revision behavior. We evaluate 19 model configurations across three text-based constraint families and find substantial cross-model and cross-constraint variation. Large revision gaps persist from the same starting responses, showing that they are not simply inherited from differences in initial generation. • A controlled analysis of feedback-to-action responses. By holding drafts fixed and varying exact correction requests, we identify reproducible, model-specific response patterns and show that post-training and model scale reshape these behaviors in different ways. These response patterns remain informative during independent multi-round revision. • A trajectory-level analysis of output recurrence and history effects. Failed revision trajectories frequently revisit earlier outputs across all three constraint families. Matched history interventions substantially alter escape from recurrence and subsequent editing behavior, while producing much smaller and heterogeneous changes in final success.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Self-Refine alternates critique and revision using the same model, without
additional training ( Madaan et al., 2023 ) . CRITIC grounds critiques
in external tool feedback ( Gou et al., 2024 ) , while SCoRe trains
multi-turn self-correction through reinforcement learning ( Kumar et al., 2025 ) . These approaches improve revision through
different feedback sources or changes to the revision policy.
Their effectiveness depends on the setting: reasoning studies find that
self-correction without external feedback can fail to improve answers ( Huang et al., 2024 ) , and code-repair studies identify feedback quality
as a limitation ( Olausson et al., 2024 ) . A broader survey likewise
emphasizes the conditions under which feedback supports correction ( Kamoi et al., 2024 ) .
Closer to our question, Feedback Friction finds that models can persist with incorrect answers despite targeted critiques generated with access to ground-truth answers ( Jiang et al., 2025 ) . RefineBench reports substantial cross-model variation in refinement performance ( Lee et al., 2026 ) .
These studies leave open whether cross-model refinement gaps persist when the starting draft and complete, exact feedback are held fixed, and whether such gaps reflect reproducible differences in how models translate the same feedback into revisions.

We study how a revision policy acts on exact feedback under standard decoding.

blocks.en: 4 Revision Performance and Feedback-to-Action Responses
blocks.zh: 4 修订业绩和反馈对行动的回应

blocks.en: 4.1 Revision Performance across Rounds and Models
blocks.zh: 4.1 各回合和模式的修订业绩

blocks.en: Table 2 shows substantial variation in final joint success even under exact feedback. API systems perform better on average than local checkpoints, but large differences remain within both groups, with controller-level mean success ranging from 17.4% to 99.8%. Performance also varies strongly across constraint families: exact-length and lexical tasks remain challenging for many models, whereas compositional tasks generally achieve higher success.

blocks.en: At the same time, this overall local–API separation is not uniform. Llama 3.1 8B, for example, reaches a mean success rate of 75.8%, matching or outperforming four of the seven API systems despite being a local 8B checkpoint. Overall, exact feedback does not eliminate substantial model- and task-dependent variation, and closed-loop revision performance does not follow a simple ordering by deployment category or nominal model scale .
blocks.zh: 同时,当地-API的这种整体分离并不统一. 例如,Llama 3.1 8B的平均成功率为75.8%,与7个API系统中的4个相匹配或胜过,尽管这是一个当地的8B检查站。 总的来说,准确的反馈并不能消除依赖模型和任务的巨大差异,闭路修改的性能也不能按照部署类别或名义模型规模的简单命令进行。

blocks.en: Figure 3 shows cumulative joint success over revision rounds 0 0 – 8 8 and reveals distinct recovery profiles across both tasks and models. Exact-length tasks benefit most visibly from repeated revision : several controllers continue to improve well into the later rounds, although the rate of recovery differs substantially across models. Some systems approach saturation after only a few revisions, while others, including Llama 3.1 8B and several API models, continue making meaningful gains near the end of the budget. Lexical tasks show a different pattern: most improvements occur in the early rounds and then diminish, leaving many models at a relatively stable plateau. Compositional tasks are more front-loaded, with many controllers already performing strongly after the first few revisions and showing little additional gain thereafter. These curves also reveal that the same revision budget has very different value across controllers: some models continue recovering from earlier failures, whereas others stop improving much earlier. Overall, models differ not only in final success, but also in the speed, persistence, and timing of recovery over repeated revisions . Detailed round-by-round results are reported in Appendix A.4 .
blocks.zh: 图3显示在修订周期0至8至8的累积联合成功,并显示不同任务和模式的回收情况。 重复修订最明显地有利于精确长的任务:若干控制器在以后几轮中继续改进,尽管不同模型的回收率差别很大。 有些系统只是在几经修订后才接近饱和,而其他系统,包括Llama 3.1 8B和几个API模型,在预算接近尾声时继续取得有意义的收益。 表征任务显示出不同的模式:大多数改进发生在早期的回合,然后逐渐减少,使许多模型留在相对稳定的高原. 组成任务更加前置,许多控制器在最初几处修改后已经表现强劲,之后几乎没有额外收益. 这些曲线还表明,同样的修订预算在控制器之间有着非常不同的价值:一些模型继续从早先的失败中恢复,而其他模型则更早停止改善. 总的来说,模式不仅在最终成功方面不同,而且在回收的速度、持久性和时间上也不同,而不是在多次修订。 附录A.4逐轮报告详细结果。

blocks.en: Are later revision gaps simply inherited from differences in initial generation ability? We test this on 240 exact-length cases, where local-model revision performance is most clearly separated. In these fixed-draft comparisons, different revisers receive the same task, initial draft, target, anchors, and revision budget, while retaining their native interfaces as in the main evaluation. Table 2 shows that, even from identical starting drafts, Llama 3.1 8B retains a 42.5–77.1 percentage-point advantage in final success across the six comparisons, all significant after Holm correction. Notably, Llama succeeds more often when revising each paired model’s drafts than when revising its own. The advantage remains 45.3–77.1 points after excluding initially successful drafts (Appendix F.1 ). Overall, large cross-model revision gaps persist even when the initial draft is held fixed, showing that they are not simply inherited from differences in initial generation .

blocks.en: Figure 4 also shows that post-training and model scale reshape revision responses in different ways. Both Llama 3.1 8B Base and Qwen3 8B Base exhibit near-zero responses over a range of deletion requests, but instruction tuning reshapes these behaviors differently. For Llama, instruction tuning largely removes this deletion-side dead zone and brings both directions closer to exact correction; for Qwen, it reduces error-expanding edits but also increases zero-action responses. Across the dense Qwen3 series from 1.7B to 32B, increasing model size does not bring responses uniformly closer to exact correction; for example, Qwen3 32B can over-correct deletion requests while still under-correcting additions. Gemma 2 9B provides a contrasting response profile, with median edits tracking the exact-correction line relatively closely in both directions. Overall, the curves reveal distinct response failures, including directional asymmetry, under-correction, and near-zero action. The Qwen3 30B-A3B MoE checkpoint provides a contrasting case, with zero median word-count change over tested requests from − 10 -10 to + 20 +20 words in both discovery and confirmation. Quantitative comparisons are in Appendix C.1 .

blocks.en: Taken together, these results reveal systematic differences in how models translate exact feedback into revision actions. Post-training can substantially reshape a shared Base-model failure pattern, but does so in checkpoint-specific ways, while increasing model scale does not consistently move responses toward exact correction ; models instead exhibit distinct patterns of under-correction, asymmetric editing, and near-zero action. Importantly, these differences extend beyond the controlled setting: across nine checkpoints, model-specific response curves reduce edit-prediction MAE on independent multi-round trajectories by 1.91 words relative to a shared curve, an 11.0% relative reduction (95% CI 8.5–13.9). Thus, feedback-to-action responses are reproducible and remain informative as revision states evolve, but better local responses alone do not determine successful closed-loop revision . Detailed comparisons and baselines are in Appendix C.1 .
blocks.zh: 总之,这些结果揭示了模型如何将准确的反馈转化为修订行动的系统性差异。 训练后可以大大改变共同的基建模式故障模式,但以检查站特定方式这样做,而不断扩大的模型规模并不能使反应向准确的校正方向发展;相反,模型显示出不同的模式,即校正不足、编辑不对称和接近零行动。 重要的是,这些差异超越了控制范围:跨越9个检查站,特定模型反应曲线将独立多轮轨道上的编辑预测MAE比共享曲线减少1.91字,相对减少11.0%(95% CI 8.5–13.9)。 因此,反馈对行动的回应是可复制的,随着修订状态的发展,信息仍然丰富,但单靠当地更好的回应不能决定成功的闭路修订。 详细比较和基线见附录C.1。

blocks.en: Prior recurrence is associated with lower subsequent recoverability. For exact-length tasks, we restrict the analysis to trajectories that remain unresolved after revision 4 and have at least one subsequent revision. We then test whether recurrence observed through revision 4 is associated with successful recovery during revisions 5–8. To distinguish this association from differences in the current revision state, we adjust for current error and missing anchors, prior error reduction and editing behavior, checkpoint, source, and length band (full specification in Appendix C.1 ).
blocks.zh: 先前的复发与随后的可恢复性较低有关。 对于精确长度的任务,我们把分析限制在修订4之后仍未解决的轨道上,并且至少有一次随后的修订. 然后,我们检验通过订正4观察到的复发是否与订正5-8期间的成功恢复有关。 为了区分这种关联与当前修订状态的差异,我们根据当前错误和缺失的锚,先前错误的减少和编辑行为,检查点,源,长度带(附录C.1中的完整规格)进行调整.

blocks.en: Table 3 shows a consistent negative association between prior recurrence and later recovery. An odds ratio below 1 indicates that trajectories with more prior repetition have lower odds of succeeding during revisions 5–8 after accounting for the measured revision state and history. In the local panel, increasing the prior repeat fraction from 0 to 1 corresponds to an adjusted odds ratio of 0.059, meaning that the estimated odds of later success fall to about 5.9% of those at the no-repeat end of the scale. The API panel shows the same pattern (OR = 0.017 =0.017 ), with a combined estimate of 0.047. All three 95% confidence intervals lie well below the no-association value of 1, with small p p values, supporting a robust negative association. The same direction is observed across most individual controllers and data sources, with additional landmark and length-subset checks reported in Appendix C.1 .

blocks.en: Recurrence therefore carries information about later recoverability even after adjustment for the measured state and history. This is a predictive association, not evidence that repetition itself causes failure. To test whether retained dialogue contributes to continued recurrence, we intervene on earlier history while holding the current draft and verifier feedback fixed, and measure subsequent revision behavior and final success separately in the next subsection.
blocks.zh: 因此,即使对所计量的状态和历史进行调整之后,再发生也包含关于以后可恢复性的信息。 这是一个预测性的联系,而不是重复本身导致失败的证据. 为了检验保留的对话是否有助于继续重现,我们干预了早先的历史,同时将目前的草案和核查反馈固定下来,并在下一小节中分别衡量随后的修订行为和最终成功.

blocks.en: 5.2 History Interventions at Matched States
blocks.zh: 5.2 相匹配国家的历史发言

blocks.en: To move from association to intervention, we compare continuations from the same recurrent state while varying only the retained dialogue history. The full-history condition preserves earlier draft–feedback pairs, whereas the reset condition removes them. The task, current draft, verifier report, decoding settings, and remaining revision budget are otherwise identical, allowing us to isolate how retained history changes subsequent revision. Our primary exact-length analysis includes 83 Llama 3.1 8B and 120 GLM-4 9B recurrent states selected at revision three or later, with over-length Llama drafts and under-length GLM drafts (Appendix C.2 ).
blocks.zh: 为了从联合转向干预,我们比较了同一经常状态的延续,而只改变了保留的对话历史。 完整的历史条件保留了早期的草稿-feedback对,而重置条件则消除了它们. 任务、目前的草案、核查报告、解码设置和剩余的修订预算在其他方面是相同的,使我们能够孤立保留的历史如何改变随后的修订。 我们的初级精确长分析包括83个Llama 3.1 8B和120个GLM-4 9B的重复状态,这些状态在修订三期或以后选定,具有超长的Llama草稿和低于长的GLM草稿(附录C.2)。

blocks.en: Removing earlier history substantially changes continuation behavior, but much less reliably improves final success. As Figure 6 shows, next-step escape increases by 42.2 percentage points for Llama and 49.2 for GLM. Correct-direction editing increases by 32.5 and 25.0 points, error contraction by 18.1 and 24.2 points, and later recurrence falls by 33.7 and 27.5 points. These changes go beyond merely producing a different output: after reset, continuations are more likely to move toward the target, reduce word-count error, and avoid returning to previously visited outputs. Yet the gains in final success are much smaller, increasing by only 10.8 points for Llama and 5.0 for GLM, to 21.7% and 8.3%, respectively. Most reset continuations therefore still fail to satisfy all constraints within the remaining budget. History removal can strongly reshape local revision behavior without producing proportionate improvements in closed-loop completion. Figure 7 broadens this result beyond the primary exact-length intervention.
blocks.zh: 消除之前的历史会大大改变延续行为,但更不可靠地改善最终的成功. 如图6所示,Llama和GLM的下一步越狱增加了42.2个百分点。 正向编辑增加32.5和25.0分,错误收缩18.1和24.2分,后来的重现下降33.7和27.5分. 这些变化不仅产生不同的产出:在重新设置后,继续更可能朝着目标前进,减少字数错误,并避免恢复以前访问的产出。 然而,最终成功的收益要小得多,Llama和GLM分别只增加了10.8个百分点和5.0个百分点,分别达到21.7%和8.3%。 因此,大多数重新设置的延续仍无法满足剩余预算的所有限制。 历史去除可以强烈地重塑局部修正行为,而不会对闭路完成产生相称的改进. 图7将这一结果扩大到主要准确长度的干预之外。

blocks.en: History effects vary across models and tasks, but local escape remains weakly coupled to completion. Across 868 matched recurrent states from Gemma, Qwen, and Falcon on lexical and compositional tasks, removing earlier dialogue changes escape from − 60.6 -60.6 to + 36.0 +36.0 percentage points across the nine model–task cells (Figure 7 a). Final-success changes are much smaller in eight of the nine cells, ranging from − 1.4 -1.4 to + 6.2 +6.2 points; the remaining Falcon sentence-length cell contains only 11 states and is reported descriptively. A 60-state GLM partial-history pilot shows the same separation: retaining progressively less dialogue raises escape from 10.0% under full history to 66.7% after reset, while final success remains between 0.0% and 5.0% (Figure 7 b). These results show that history removal can help or hinder recurrence escape depending on the model and task, while large local changes need not translate into comparable gains in completion. The direction also depends on the trigger-state composition: excluding first-revision repeats reverses some escape effects (Appendix F.3 ).

blocks.en: Taken together, the matched-state experiments show that retained dialogue is part of the effective revision state: changing history can substantially alter continuation behavior even when the current draft and feedback are fixed. History therefore shapes closed-loop dynamics, but manipulating history alone is not sufficient to make revision reliable. Full cross-task results, paired partial-history contrasts, and trigger-state sensitivity are reported in Appendices C.3 , C.4 , and F.3 . Appendix D reports supplementary internal-model analyses.
blocks.zh: 组合起来,匹配状态实验显示,保留对话是有效修订状态的一部分:即使当前草稿和反馈固定下来,改变历史也能实质性改变延续行为. 因此,历史塑造了闭路动态,但仅仅操纵历史并不足以使修订工作可靠。 完整的跨任务结果,配对部分历史对比,以及触发状态敏感性在附录C.3,C.4,和F.3中报告. 附录D报告补充内部模型分析。

blocks.en: 6 Discussion and Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6. 讨论和结论

blocks.en: Taken together, our results suggest that closed-loop revision should be understood as a property of the interaction between the model and its evolving revision state, rather than of feedback quality alone. Once feedback correctness and completeness are held fixed, substantial differences remain across models and constraints, persist from matched starting drafts, and appear as reproducible feedback-to-action response patterns. These differences do not follow a simple ordering by model scale or deployment category. At the trajectory level, recurrent outputs mark states with lower subsequent recoverability, while matched-history interventions show that changing retained dialogue can strongly alter local continuation behavior without reliably improving final completion. The same intervention can even help or hinder recurrence escape across models and tasks. Together, these findings separate three notions that are often conflated in iterative revision: observing the error, translating feedback into an effective action, and reliably completing the loop.
blocks.zh: 我们的结果表明,闭关修订应被理解为模型与其不断演变的修订状态之间相互作用的一部分,而不是仅仅作为反馈质量的一部分。 一旦将反馈正确性和完整性固定下来,模型和制约因素之间仍然存在巨大差异,从匹配的起始稿一直存在,并似乎是可复制的反馈与行动反应模式。 这些差异并非按照模型规模或部署类别简单排序。 在轨迹方面,经常产出标志着后续可恢复性较低的状态,而相应的历史干预表明,改变保留的对话可以强烈改变当地继续行为,而不会可靠地改进最后完成。 同样的干预甚至可以帮助或阻碍各种模式和任务的重复。 这些结论共同分离了经常被混入迭代修订的三个概念:观察错误,将反馈转化为有效的行动,可靠地完成循环.

blocks.en: Evaluation should therefore consider not only endpoint success or single-step improvement, but also consistent feedback incorporation, recurrence, and retained history. More broadly, improvements at one stage need not propagate to end-to-end completion: changing history can substantially alter local revision behavior with much smaller gains in final success. Our fixed-budget, deterministically checkable text tasks do not cover subjective objectives, incomplete feedback, or changing environments. Within this scope, exact feedback provides observability, not control: reliable closed-loop revision requires models whose responses remain effective as the revision state evolves.
blocks.zh: 因此,评价不仅应考虑结束点的成功或单步骤的改进,而且应考虑连贯的反馈纳入、重复和保留历史。 更广泛地说,一个阶段的改进不需要推广到端到端的完成:改变历史可以大幅度改变地方修正行为,最终成功的收益要小得多。 我们的固定预算,决定性的可核对文本任务,并不涵盖主观目标,不完整的反馈,或者不断变化的环境. 在这个范围内,精确的反馈提供了可观察性,而不是控制性:可靠的闭路修正需要模型,其反应随着修正状态的演化依然有效.

Appendix D Aligned Checkpoint Localization

This supplementary study uses Llama as a worked example and includes
aligned Qwen3 8B and Gemma 2 9B checkpoints, with the
input interface held fixed within each pair. The studies test error readout,
Base-weight restoration into Instruct, activation transplantation, and
Instruct-weight grafts into Base. They do not assume that corresponding
layer ranges implement the same function across architectures.

Causal tracing ( Meng et al., 2022 ) , activation patching ( Zhang and Nanda, 2024 ) , and weight grafting ( Nief et al., 2025 ) provide tools for locating information and
testing how model components affect behavior.
Work on subspace choice ( Makelov et al., 2024 ) and interactions among
mediators ( Vaidyanathan et al., 2026 ) shows how intervention design
affects causal attribution.
We use probes and interventions to examine error information and revision
behavior, with an aligned Llama Base–Instruct pair as the main case and
complementary Gemma and Qwen interventions.
We evaluate individual edits and complete revision trajectories separately
to determine whether changes in local behavior accompany gains in final
success.
D.1 Operations and Readout Conventions

A block is one decoder layer, indexed from zero: blocks 0–31 in Llama,
0–35 in Qwen, and 0–41 in Gemma. A block intervention selects every
checkpoint tensor under model.layers.{i}.* , including the
attention, MLP, and within-block normalization parameters. The output
package separately selects model.norm.* and lm_head.* .
Unselected tensors retain the recipient checkpoint’s values.

We read the representation at the final prompt token, before generating
an edit, from the model’s returned hidden_states tuple.
Probe labels L0, L1, … index this tuple, whose first entry is the
embedding representation; they are not zero-based parameter-block labels.
The prespecified readouts are L32 for Llama, L36 for Qwen, and L42 for
Gemma. We standardize features using the training split and fit ridge
readouts for error sign and required-correction magnitude (2 versus 10
words). Regularization is selected by case-grouped cross-validation on
discovery data and frozen before confirmation. Readability does not
establish that generation uses the decoded information.

Restoration uses Instruct as recipient and Base as donor. For each
selected tensor, half restoration sets θ ′ = 0.5 ​ θ Instruct + 0.5 ​ θ Base \theta^{\prime}=0.5\theta_{\mathrm{Instruct}}+0.5\theta_{\mathrm{Base}} ;
interpolation is computed in float32 and cast back to the recipient dtype.
Full restoration copies the Base tensor, while sham preserves Instruct
weights. Half restoration mixes every selected tensor, rather than
replacing half the selected blocks. Grafting reverses the direction:
selected Instruct tensors replace their counterparts in a Base recipient.
These are weight interventions, without additional training.

This operation instead replaces donor activations in a recipient forward
pass on identical tokenized inputs. The Llama experiments intervene on
post-block residuals over the feedback-message span during prompt prefill,
in both Base-to-Instruct and Instruct-to-Base directions; generated-token
states are untouched. The subsections below specify the sites, samples,
and behavioral criteria for each experiment.

For Qwen and Gemma, fixed-state discovery uses 24 cases (96 states), and
confirmation uses 48 disjoint cases (192 states). The 480-case closed-loop

D.6 Llama Controller Graft

Five Base-recipient conditions share the Meta interface and greedy decoding:
sham, blocks 8–15, output package, their joint graft, and a matched
noncontiguous-plus-output control. Each runs 96 fixed states and Main-120;

against both Base and the noncontiguous-plus-output control; the observed

therefore does not meet the criterion for transferring effective revision

On the 96 fixed states, direction accuracy is 25.0% for Base,
59.4% with the block graft, 46.9% with the output graft, and 81.25%
with their joint graft. The joint graft succeeds on 10 of 120 separate

Qwen3 8B Base and Instruct share a 36-block architecture and the same
Instruct serialization. Tokenizer and tensor-shape audits pass. Probe
regularization is selected using discovery cases and frozen before
confirmation (Table 19 ). Error direction remains
readable in both checkpoints. Error expansion denotes an increase in
absolute word-count error after an edit, | d t + 1 | > | d t | |d_{t+1}|>|d_{t}| . The stored
fields call this outcome overshoot (or its complement overshoot_avoidance ); it need not involve crossing the target.

The restoration screen tests four nine-block bands, the output package,
a sham, and a parameter-count-matched noncontiguous control. Blocks 0–8
and 9–17 are selected in discovery. On the 192 held-out fixed states,
full restoration increases error expansion by 62.0 and 21.4 percentage points,
respectively; paired 95% intervals are [50.0, 72.9] and [10.9, 32.8].
Half-restoration effects are weaker. Both groups satisfy the frozen
restoration criteria, including comparison with the noncontiguous control.
